newsitem.title: USA: Lipper sees 10-12 pct returns for U.S. funds.
newsitem.headline: Lipper sees 10-12 pct returns for U.S. funds.

text.p: U.S. stock mutual funds should return between 10 and 12 percent annually in the next several years after gaining an average 19.47 percent in 1996, fund tracker Michael Lipper predicted Friday.

"Going forward, one would expect domestic stock fund performance to return to more normal levels after the torrid pace of the last couple of years," said Lipper, president of Lipper Analytical Services.
"That would suggest returns will fall back into the 10 percent to 12 percent range over the next several years," Lipper said.
Lipper said the outlook for this year is "for mildly good domestic returns at best."

He said world equity and balanced funds, which include stocks and bonds, "could well have their day in the sun, unless a market downturn makes money market and high-quality bond funds look attractive."
Lipper said U.S. stocks funds rose an average 4.99 percent in the fourth quarter, with index funds gaining 8.22 percent and growth funds up 5.14 percent.
Among foreign sectors, Japanese funds were losers, falling 9.77 percent, while Latin American funds were up 2.12 percent.
Noting that funds benefitted from the October-November stock market rally, Lipper wondered "whether we will pay for it in January."
With the 31.08 percent gain in U.S. stock funds in 1995, the general stock fund sector has returned more than 56 percent in the last two years.

Lipper said historical data indicate that declines have followed two full years of increases. He noted that after the strong performances in 1967-68, funds dropped 12.67 percent in 1969 and 7.22 percent in 1970.
The average world equity fund gained three percent in the fourth quarter, with European funds rising 8.70 percent.

Lipper said investing in overseas funds and securities provided a hedge against U.S. securities. He said that over the last 35 years, world equity funds outperformed U.S. stock funds 11.52 percent versus 10.78 percent.

According to Lipper, the top five performers for the 1996 year were: State Street Research Global Resources A shares, up 70.25 percent; Van Kampen American Growth A shares, up 61.99 percent; Interactive Investors Technology Value, up 60.91 percent; Portico Microcap Institutional, up 57.23 percent; and State State Research Aurora Class C, up 56.88 percent.

The trailing five were: Matthews International Korea, down 31.79 percent; Steadman Technology and Growth, down 30.36 percent; U.S. Services Gold Shares, down 25.49 percent; Fidelity Japan Small Company, off 24.59 percent; and Bhirud Apex Mid-Cap Growth, off 23.01 percent, according to Lipper.
